subject: URGENT: Ingress prefix drop in SDK causing 502s and p95 latency spike
messages:
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@crestline-retail.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: elena@crestline-retail.com
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production errors after SDK rollout

Olga,

We're seeing a big regression in production since we flipped to the new Redwood client SDK this morning. p95 token latency climbed from ~120ms to ~1.4s and we're getting intermittent 502s on generation calls. The errors seem correlated with high concurrency on our checkout path.

Attached are a short HAR and a small log of headers from a few failed requests (client-sdk-headers.log.txt). The backend traces show requests missing the expected x-rd-prefixed metadata header ("x-rd-prefix") on the failing calls.

Elena and I are ready to provide access to traces or run a quick rollback if that's the recommended mitigation. This is impacting checkout success on a holiday promo — we need immediate help.

--
Sam Rivera
Sr. Engineering Manager, Crestline Retail
sam.rivera@crestline-retail.com

Subject: Re: Production errors after SDK rollout

Thanks Sam — I'm looking into this now and have escalated to our on-call infra team.

Immediate asks so we can triage faster:
- Can you confirm whether you are using the v2.1.0 SDK (the rollout today) or an earlier pinned version?
- If you can, send one full raw request/response pair (headers + body) for a failing call. The attached client log is helpful.

We will evaluate rollback to the previous client codepath if we cannot get a fix in 30–45 minutes. Marissa/Sean/Jonas, loop in infra/runtime.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors after SDK rollout

Olga / team — thanks for the ping. Early suspicion: the SDK's streaming parser appears to aggressively trim leading whitespace on the first chunk when a connection reuses a pooled stream, which causes the upstream router to drop the custom "x-rd-prefix" header when header folding occurs. That would explain missing metadata and a fraction of calls failing with 502 (router rejects the request for missing routing header) and higher latency due to retries and backlog.

I've attached a small repro log from our staging harness and a trace snippet (client-sdk-headers.log.txt). Action plan:
1) Add a temporary guard in the SDK to preserve exact first-chunk bytes (disable the aggressive trim) and publish a hotfix v2.1.1.
2) As a short mitigation, recommend Crestline flip traffic back to the non-SDK HTTP path (we can provide a toggle) while the hotfix deploys to avoid further revenue impact.

I'll start a Jira (JIRA-INC-4321) and aim to have a hotfix within 90 minutes. If we need to, we can also push an emergency canary and then a global patch.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber, Runtime Engineering
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
From: Elena Varela <elena@crestline-retail.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@crestline-retail.com>
Cc: Crestline Execs <execs@crestline-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors after SDK rollout

Olga,

Thanks for the quick reply. We're on v2.1.0 (just released this morning). Traffic is already degraded — checkout conversions dropped ~18% in the last 30 minutes. Our CTO is copied here; they're asking for an immediate mitigation approach short of a full service rollback.

If the toggle to route off the SDK is straightforward, please send steps and expected blast radius. We need something that doesn't add more risk to the checkout flow.

—Elena
Elena Varela
VP Product, Crestline Retail
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Varela <elena@crestline-retail.com>, Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@crestline-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 10:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production errors after SDK rollout

Elena / Sam — immediate mitigation plan below. We're treating this as a Sev A and I'm routing to Execs internally for notification.

Mitigation (short timeframe):
- Toggle: We can flip Crestline traffic to the direct HTTP integration (bypassing the SDK) via the dashboard toggle (Route Policy > Client Adapters > Use Direct HTTP). Effect: will remove the SDK from the request path; expected recovery within 90–120s after toggle propagation. Blast radius: only requests from the app instances using the SDK toggle will change; we will coordinate a full-switchover of the checkout pool.
- Hotfix: Jonas will ship SDK v2.1.1 to disable aggressive trimming of first-chunk whitespace and add strict header-preservation tests. Target deploy: 90 minutes.
- Monitoring: We'll create a dedicated dashboard and an alert on x-rd-prefix missing-rate and p95 token latency.

If you approve the toggle, we will schedule the change and send a step-by-step runbook and a support engineer to watch the roll.

—Olga

Subject: Re: Production errors after SDK rollout — resolution and next steps

Sam / Elena — follow-up and status update.

What we did:
- At 10:48 PT on 2027-11-03 we flipped Crestline off the SDK path to direct HTTP via the dashboard toggle. Checkout error rate dropped to baseline within ~75s and p95 recovered to ~140ms.
- Jonas pushed SDK v2.1.1 to our canary cluster at 11:25 PT and it preserved the header in our canary harness. We rolled v2.1.1 to global at 13:10 PT after a 45 minute canary with no regressions.
- We validated Crestline's production traces and confirmed x-rd-prefix is present on requests post-fix.

Next steps:
- Postmortem and root cause writeup (JIRA-INC-4321) — Jonas will own the technical RCA and I will draft the customer-facing incident report. Target: EOD 2027-11-05.
- We will add an integration test for header-preservation across pooled-stream reuse cases and include it in the SDK CI gate.
- Compensation: Marissa will coordinate a goodwill credit for the promo hour impact and Sean will follow up on SLA credits if applicable.

Attachments: prod-p95-graph.png (p95 before/after), client-sdk-headers.log.txt, har_capture.har

We're sorry for the disruption and appreciate the fast coordination. I will send the postmortem link when it's ready.

—Olga Petrov
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
